# Fixture provenance

Every `.dts` and `.dsq` here is generated by `build_fixtures.py` from the
example shapes — the four `.blend` files committed under `examples/`, and the
fifteen showcase ones `examples/build_examples.py` builds from nothing as it
goes.  Nothing in this directory is game data.

```sh
blender --background --factory-startup --python tests/fixtures/build_fixtures.py
```

The `.png` files are copies of `examples/mod/DtsExamples/textures/`, put here
because the engine — and the importer — find a material's texture by its name
next to the shape.  `crt_monitor/` is the one shape exported *with* its textures
into a directory of its own, including the IFL frames under `skins/`.

## Why they are generated

They used to be shapes lifted out of Tribes 2 and the Torque SDK.  That bought
one thing and cost another, and the trade has been reversed.

**What generating them costs.**  A reader test that reads a file this library
wrote is checking the pair against itself, not against the format.  Nothing here
can catch the two halves agreeing on something the engine does not do.

Two things make that affordable.  The corpus tests
(`tests/test_roundtrip_corpus.py`, `tests/blender/roundtrip_sweep.py`) run
against the real game data on a machine that has it — 867 shapes and 1709
sequences on this one — and they are the check against the format.
`scripts/mutate.py` is the other half: break the writer and a fixture-backed
test still has to notice.

**What it buys.**  A checkout with no game bytes in it, and a fixture whose
source is a `.blend` in the same repository — so "why does this file have a
sorted mesh" has an answer you can open.

## Reading the names

`v<version>_<shape>` — the DTS or DSQ version, then the shape it came from with
its number dropped.  `v19_sorted_foliage.dts` is `build_examples.py`'s
`03_sorted_foliage` exported as v19.

The number is dropped because it is not part of a shape's identity.  Two sets
feed this directory and both number from 1: the four hand-made `.blend` files
committed under `examples/`, and the fifteen one-feature showcase shapes
`examples/build_examples.py` builds from nothing into a scratch directory.
`build_fixtures.py` takes the slug-to-number map from those two builders rather
than repeating it, so a renumbering on either side cannot leave this file
pointing at a shape that moved.

Every shape but one is exported at v24.  The older versions are chosen for the
format feature each one is the last or first to have; `build_fixtures.py` says
which, per entry, and that comment is the reason the fixture exists.

## What is *not* generated

Some tests need a shape no version of this add-on will ever write — a merge
index table, a mesh whose flags echo its type, two decals sharing a name, an
object resting at vis 0, a matters bit naming an object the shape lacks, a decal
coverage list the default rule cannot reproduce.  Those are seeded inside the
test that needs them: read a fixture, set the field, write it back, import that.
Each one says so, and says why nothing writes it.

This is the sharp edge of generating the fixtures, and it does not announce
itself.  Four tests went silently vacuous on the change — they still passed,
still read as if they asserted something, and the suite was green — because the
shape they had been asking the question of no longer had the property in it.
`scripts/mutate.py` is what found all four.  Run it after touching anything
here.

## The shape that is not a fixture

`examples/04_light_male.blend` is an example and is deliberately not exported
into this directory.  It is the largest shape in the repository and the only
one with a real animation library on it, so it would be a useful fixture — but
it is an import of a retail Tribes 2 player, and the sentence at the top of
this file saying nothing here is game data is worth more than one more shape to
reach for.  `NOT_A_FIXTURE` in `build_fixtures.py` is where that is enforced.
The corpus tests already cover everything it would have been reached for.

## One import

`examples/02_tutorial_player.blend` is not authored.  It is an import of the
Torque SDK's own tutorial player — `player.dts` and the `.dsq` set beside it in
`agentic-torque/mygame/animation-test/data/shapes/tutorial-player/` — kept
because it is the only 45-node, 13-sequence shape available and the DSQ and
matters-set tests want one.  Its `player_blue.jpg` is packed into the `.blend`.
The two fixtures from it (`v23_tutorial_player.dts`, `v24_tutorial_player.dts`,
`v24_tutorial_player.dsq`) therefore carry SDK sample content, which is worth
knowing before this directory is described as clean.
